findings.title: Client deletion fails under V2 because the removal listener calls an unimplemented V2 method
findings.body: The ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, and this PR makes clients() return ClientPermissionsV2. Its setPermissionsEnabled (ClientPermissionsV2.java:193) throws UnsupportedOperationException. The exception propagates out of event publishing, so deleting any client fails when the V1 flag is also enabled. The V1 flag gate on the listener (line 77) hides this for V2-only deployments instead of fixing it. No test in the PR deletes a client under V2, so the regression is not caught.

findings.title: Removal cleanup is gated on the V1 feature flag, disabling it entirely for V2-only deployments
findings.body: The whole listener is now wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), the V1 flag. The base code had no guard, so under V2-only the role, group and client removal handlers ran through management(), which selects V2. With this change they never run when only V2 is enabled. Permission state for deleted roles, groups and clients is then left behind. The guard appears to be a workaround for the exception in the ClientRemovedEvent branch, not a fix. The guard should check the feature actually in use, and the V2 client cleanup should be implemented or explicitly made a no-op.

findings.title: All-clients grants are ignored for any client that has its own resource
findings.body: hasPermission(client, scope) only consults the 'Clients' type resource when no per-client resource exists. If a per-client permission exists for client A (for example CONFIGURE), then canManage(A), canConfigure(A), canMapRoles(A), canMapCompositeRoles(A) and canMapClientScopeRoles(A) evaluate only A's resource. An all-clients MANAGE or MAP_ROLES grant is therefore silently ignored for A but honored for every other client. This contradicts the Javadoc added in ClientPermissionEvaluator ('For V2 only: Also if the caller has a permission to ... all clients'). It is also inconsistent with canView(client), which checks the all-clients VIEW grant unconditionally via canView(). No test combines a per-client permission with an all-clients permission for clients, so this is not covered.

findings.title: Null dereference when the 'Clients' type resource does not exist
findings.body: getResourceTypeResource(...) returns null when the 'Clients' resource type resource is absent from the store, or when the schema does not apply. That null is passed straight to getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a check. The absence is realistic for realms whose admin permissions were initialized before this change, because init() never adds the Clients resource (see AdminPermissionsSchema.java:226). Any per-client permission check for a client without its own resource then fails with an NPE instead of returning false.

findings.title: No upgrade path for realms already initialized before the Clients type and scopes existed
findings.body: init() returns early when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, so realms initialized before this change never receive the new Clients resource type or the new scopes configure, map-roles-client-scope and map-roles-composite. Creating a client permission in such a realm then fails in getOrCreateResource (line 108) with ModelException 'No scopes found.', and read paths hit the null type resource in ClientPermissionsV2 line 219. The PR needs a sync step for missing resource types and scopes, or it must explain why existing realms are unsupported.

findings.title: Authorization queries throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning a decision
findings.body: canExchangeTo is an authorization decision, yet it throws. The same is true of isPermissionsEnabled (line 188), getPermissions (line 203) and the mapRoles/manage/configure/view Policy factories. MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns this class, so callers that previously received the inherited V1 behaviour now get a server error on these paths. The PR does not show that these callers are unreachable under V2. Returning false, or implementing the method, would be safer than a 500.

findings.title: getResourceName has no mapping for Clients resources
findings.body: For the USERS type, getResourceName maps the internal id to a readable username. For the CLIENTS type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not derived from the client. Resources for clients are named with the client's internal UUID, so the result will not identify the client by clientId. The USERS branch shows the intended behaviour and the CLIENTS case is missing.

findings.title: requireView() Javadoc describes a boolean return for a void method
findings.body: The Javadoc for requireView() says 'Returns true if canView() returns true', but the method is void and should throw ForbiddenException when canView() is false. The same mistake appears in the Javadoc for requireViewClientScopes() (line 101). Both were added in this PR and should describe the throw behaviour, as the requireX methods above them do.

findings.title: Dead getEvaluationContext method and unused imports copied from V1
findings.body: getEvaluationContext is private and never called, since canExchangeTo throws. Its supporting imports (ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, EvaluationContext) exist only for it. The logger field (line 51), the TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import (line 46) and the Scope import (line 27) are also unused. This is leftover copy-paste that will confuse maintainers about what V2 actually supports.
